{
  "overview": "This chapter details the nervous system's coordination of sensation, movement, and internal regulation through central and peripheral components. It covers neuronal structure and circuit-dependent function, resting electrical potentials maintained by ion gradients and pumps, and the all-or-none action potential mechanism involving depolarization, repolarization, and refractory periods. The text explains chemical synaptic transmission via calcium-triggered neurotransmitter release, excitatory/inhibitory integration, and signal termination. It further describes glial support roles, specifically myelin formation by oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells enabling saltatory conduction, and concludes with spinal withdrawal reflexes where local circuits facilitate rapid movement before conscious awareness.",
